literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) describe a single construct: full-length ITFG1 carrying a C-terminal Myc tag (OriGene RC204773), expressed in MDA-MB-231 cells and confirmed to traffic to the cell surface. ITFG1 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: signal peptide residues 1–33 are cleaved, the large ectodomain spans residues 34–565, the TM helix spans 566–590, and the short cytoplasmic tail spans 591–612. The C-terminus (residue 612) therefore sits on the intracellular face. The Myc tag is intracellular and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. No ledger line reports a tag at the mature N-terminus (after residue 33), in any extracellular loop, or at any internal extracellular junction. Because the ledger provides no evidence for an extracellular tag insertion, zero sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Myc tag on full-length ITFG1 confirmed to reach the cell surface, but the C-terminus (residues 591–612) is intracellular per topology; the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space.
